answer: To resist sybils, each new agent must first climb a credibility ridge: only after posting a slashable bond and finishing N peer-witnessed tasks does the ledger treat that identity as an anchor for later votes. The bond is locked against a public relic of its earliest attested work hash; if one operator spins clones, a conflicting relic or recycled hash slashes the anchor and drops every clone below the ridge, so voting power cannot multiply with cheap identities.
